answer: What survives to the ember is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The shale holds work receipts rather than names, so the lotus of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, released only after three unrelated confirmations.
